I haven't passed. All three submissions are used and the last review failed, so I can't submit again.

- **Submission 1:** failed the overload test. A string cable overheated before its fuse operated. The C-95 cable's derated ampacity was only just equal to the 250 A fuse rating, which does not leave enough margin for the fuse's conventional fusing current.
- **Submission 2:** fixed that by moving to C-120. It then failed the commercial review: a competing design meets the same requirements for significantly less.

The submitted design was 368 cells in series, 15 strings in parallel, 3 × PCS-1, TX-3, FU-13, CT-2, C-120 (single pair), 7 × CU-1, RMU-6, with no deviations.

The report doesn't say where the cheaper design saves money. I was too conservative in these places, and each would likely have cut cost:
- **Cell count:** 384 × 14 (5,376 cells) instead of 368 × 15 saves about 11k. My energy model had almost no margin there (3,450.04 kWh against 3,450 required), so I wasn't sure the lab would accept it.
- **DC cable:** two parallel C-50 pairs per string instead of one C-120 would save about 10k. It still meets the ampacity needed for the fuse coordination (about 305 A against about 276 A).
- **Cooling units:** I sized heating to hold cells at 25 °C at −15 °C ambient. Holding 20 °C would allow 6 × CU-1 and save about 10k.

Together these would be roughly 30k on a total of about 830k, which may or may not be enough to get within 5% of the cheapest design.
